primitives.note: Q passive: on-hit bonus magic damage based on target max health, plus cooldown reduction
Each Q cast arms the next basic attack with bonus effect (cone/tail slam/bite)
All Emberstrike-empowered attacks reset the basic attack timer
Q: chained recasts (2 in human, 3 in dragon form); W: shield then recast explosion
On-hit attacks reduce Q's current cooldown by 0.5s
Q passive and E damage scale off target's max health
Dragon Form scorched ground field deals damage over time
R transforms Shyvana into Dragon Form, empowering Q/W/E with additional effects and higher damage
Dragon Fury resource gates R cast and Dragon Form duration; generated by passive regen, attacks, and ability hits
Scalemail stacks grant armor/MR, but not obtainable in a 1v1 dummy fight (no takedowns) - likely irrelevant to damage fight
W grants bonus move speed for a duration (does not affect damage fight; movement ignored)
Q1/Q2 primary target damage can crit; Q3 true damage cannot crit
Q cone/AoE secondary hits, W explosion radius, E fireball/explosion/scorched field all assume single-target dummy positioning
W shield and Dragon Form heal, and Scalemail resists, only matter for damage taken, not the damage-dealing fight

needsBespoke.why: Shyvana's Q is a chained recast system where only the FINAL cast in a chain puts the basic attack on cooldown (others are free resets), and the chain length itself changes depending on form (2 casts human, 3 casts dragon, with the 3rd being true damage that can't crit) - this multi-stage conditional attack-reset/recast interaction is more complex than a single generic primitive captures. Additionally Dragon Fury as a resource is generated by a passive regen tick, by attacks, and by ability hits (with different multipliers in/out of Dragon Form and vs champions/monsters), which is a bespoke resource-generation model beyond a simple resource-budget primitive, and determines how many times R (and thus Dragon Form empowerment of Q/W/E) can be triggered inside the 15s fight.

unsettled.question: How long can Shyvana sustain Dragon Form in the fight, given Fury generation from attacks/ability hits on a single target plus passive regen, and how many times can R itself be recast (it requires 100 Fury to cast again)?
options: Only casts R once (starts with 100 Fury from learning it, insufficient regen to recast within 15s)
Can recast R once or more within 15s depending on attack speed/haste, since attacks and ability hits during Dragon Form generate Fury at 3x rate
Sim should assume a fixed number of Dragon Form entries as a rotation parameter

She maintains {{sbc|Dragon Form}} at a recurring cost of {{as|Dragon Fury}}, returning to {{sbc|Human Form}} once all {{as|Dragon Fury}} has been depleted.

unsettled.question: In the 15s damage fight, does Shyvana's Q chain (cast Q repeatedly to get empowered attacks) actually only consume ONE real cooldown per chain (since only the last cast in the chain goes on cooldown), meaning she can throw out 2 (human) or 3 (dragon) empowered attacks per ~6-10s cooldown window?
options: Yes - simulate exactly as wiki states: intermediate casts are free, only the final cast per chain starts the real cooldown
No - some hidden internal cooldown between individual Q casts within a chain limits how fast the chain can be executed, effectively capping DPS gain

This results in the same functionality as {{cai|Shield of Daybreak|Leona}} and {{cai|Thundering Smash|Volibear}}, effectively being a triple/quintuple attack reset.

options: Passive on-hit damage always applies alongside the empowered attack's own damage (stacking)
Empowered attacks replace the normal on-hit passive proc entirely

unsettled.question: Does W's damage-only recast explosion trigger automatically and reliably within the 15s window (auto-triggers after 1s+ or when shield breaks/expires), or does optimal play require manually delaying/holding it, affecting how many W damage instances land in 15s?
options: Always recast/explode as soon as possible (1s after cast) to maximize W casts per 15s
Hold the shield full duration (2.5s) before it auto-explodes, reducing total W casts per 15s

unsettled.question: In Dragon Form, does E's subsequent-explosion 40% damage penalty apply to the dummy on every recast of E against the same stationary target (since it never leaves the scorched field), effectively reducing all but the first E cast's damage in the fight?
options: Yes - all but the first E hit on the dummy within the field's lifetime take 40% damage
No - if the scorched field expires (2s duration) before the next E cast, full damage applies each time since cooldown (8-12s) exceeds field duration
quotes: Enemies may be damaged by only one scorched field at a time. Subsequent explosions against the same target deal {{ap|{{#var:xpl}}*100}}% damage.

proposal: Start in Human Form, apply Scalemail is irrelevant (no takedowns available); begin auto-attacking the dummy immediately.
Cast R (Dragon's Descent) as soon as available (100 Fury from learning it) to enter Dragon Form and get the R cast magic damage plus empower Q/W/E.

While in Dragon Form, weave Q (Emberstrike) on cooldown: cast Q, let the empowered attack land (resets attack timer), recast Q for the 2nd empowered attack, recast again for the 3rd (true damage bite) before the chain's real cooldown starts.
Cast E (Molten Burst) on cooldown, positioning so the fireball explosion and the resulting scorched field both hit the dummy for the DoT.
Cast W (Inferno Aegis) on cooldown, holding it as briefly as possible before recasting for the explosion damage (and Dragon Form heal, though the heal doesn't matter in the damage-only fight).
Continue auto-attacking between ability casts (basic attacks add on-hit Q passive magic damage and generate Fury to sustain Dragon Form).
Attempt to keep recasting R when Fury permits, to maximize Dragon Form uptime and its accompanying empowered Q/W/E effects and the flat R damage per cast.
Maintain this Q/W/E/attack loop on cooldown for the full 15 seconds, prioritizing whichever ability is off cooldown, with Q taking priority due to its added on-hit passive and attack resets.
questions: Should the simulator model Dragon Form Fury explicitly (regen + attack/ability generation), or assume a simplified fixed number of R casts and permanent Dragon Form for the fight duration?
Is there a real minimum gap between chained Q casts (human-perceptible input delay) that would cap how many empowered Q attacks land in 15s, beyond the stated 4-6s windows?
Given Q1/Q2 crit but Q3 (true damage) does not, should the optimal build prioritize crit itemization, and how should the sim value the mixed crit/non-crit Q chain?

Should W's recast be assumed instant (to maximize its own cast frequency) or delayed to let the shield value show up in survival-fight-style bonus health interactions (not relevant here since this is the damage fight)?

Does the E scorched field's persistent damage stack with (or get overwritten by) a fresh E cast's explosion damage on the same target within the field's 2s lifetime, given E's own cooldown (8-12s) usually exceeds the field duration?
